reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence. The key premises rely entirely on standard textbook knowledge of aluminizing and alumina formation on conventional alloys, but the specific claim about the behavior of a multicomponent HEA bond coat under these conditions is unsupported by any cited data.
premises: Aluminizing via pack cementation can enrich the surface of an alloy with aluminum.
The introduced aluminum will react with oxygen to form a thermodynamically stable, slow-growing, and adherent alumina (Al2O3) scale.
This alumina scale acts as a barrier to further oxidation and reduces spallation.
The multicomponent nature of the HEA will not fundamentally prevent the formation of a protective, continuous alumina scale.
